items.title: RVSD: Retrieval Vision Sparse Decoding for Mitigating Visual Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces RVSD, a training-free decoding framework to combat visual hallucinations in large vision-language models. RVSD unifies token sparsification and semantic-space visual retrieval within a single pass, using a semantics-directed strategy to select important tokens and an on-demand retrieval mechanism for visual compensation. This approach aims to reduce computational overhead compared to existing methods.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of representative paradigms for mitigating VHs in LVLMs: (a) training-based alignment and RAG ( Sun et al., 2024 ) , (b) decoding interventions ( Leng et al., 2024 ; Favero et al., 2024 ) , (c) sparse decoders ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) , and (d) our RVSD, which turns pruned tokens into a retrievable memory bank and restores grounding on demand in a single forward pass.

items.title: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.abstract: This paper models multi-agent LLM systems as a bilevel coordination game, where the orchestrator and workers engage in strategic interaction. It analyzes reflection as a process of improving semantic memory and proves theoretical bounds on its effectiveness. The key contribution is an information-theoretic result showing that external grounding is crucial for effective coordination in such systems.
items.figure_caption: Bilevel coordinated reflection. The orchestrator (leader) selects a decomposition \( \tau \) and updates strategy memory m o m_{o} on the slower timescale; workers (followers) update execution memory m e m_{e} via \( \eta_{c} \) -better responses on the faster timescale. Under bounded coupling, the followers’ subgame is an approximate potential game with slack η c ≤ 2 ​ d max ​ \( \eta_{c} \)\( \leq \) 2d_{\( \max \)}\( \kappa \) , while verifier-gated SRMA separately governs which memory proposals are committed.

items.title: DKL: Decoupled Knowledge Learning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces Decoupled Knowledge Learning (DKL) to improve instruction-tuned language models with new knowledge. DKL addresses limitations of existing methods by performing extended pre-training on the base LLM, not the instruction-tuned one. This approach injects knowledge without degrading instruction-following abilities and avoids the need for extensive synthetic data or costly re-instruction tuning.

items.title: From Tokens to Semantics: Leveraging Complementary Signals for Hallucination Detection in Black-Box LLMs
items.abstract: This paper proposes a method to detect hallucinations in black-box LLMs by combining two complementary signals: semantic entropy (response meaning disagreement) and token uncertainty. Their novel "TopK" method enhances token uncertainty detection by aggregating signals across multiple sampled responses. The proposed "CoCoA" and "Gated" methods leverage these signals to improve hallucination detection accuracy, especially in cases where individual signals might fail.

items.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
items.abstract: SafeEvolve proposes an experience-driven framework for LLM agent safety alignment. It achieves this by co-evolving the agent's harness (e.g., prompts, skills) and policy based on safety experiences from completed trajectories. This continuous loop allows for bounded, auditable harness updates and improved policy safety through staged fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
items.figure_caption: Conceptual motivation of SafeEvolve. Harness-only evolution can exceed policy capacity and yield fragile control, while policy-only evolution transfers poorly and misses emerging failures. SafeEvolve couples harness refinement with policy updates in a co-evolutionary loop.

items.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
items.abstract: This paper investigates how large language models' medical reasoning is corrupted by misleading context. The core method involves injecting fabricated evidence and bare assertions into medical questions and analyzing model susceptibility, disclosure of misleading cues, and reasoning mechanisms. The key contribution is demonstrating that models are more vulnerable to bare assertions than fabricated evidence, and while misleading cues are often disclosed in reasoning traces, they are less frequently revealed in the final responses.
items.figure_caption: The injection design and its behavioral effect. (a) All five arms share a clean stem, differing only in one appended sentence. (b) Uptake of the option each cue endorses, by arm and model. The dashed line marks the clean base rate. Error bars are 95 % 95\% item-bootstrap CIs.

items.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
items.abstract: This paper introduces EarlyEval, a method to significantly reduce the cost of evaluating LLM agents. Instead of running full evaluations, EarlyEval uses lightweight classifiers to predict the final outcome based on intermediate agent behavior. This allows for early termination of runs, saving computational resources and cost without compromising evaluation accuracy.

items.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a new training objective called "predicted-state matching" for web agents. Instead of simply predicting the next web state, this method trains world models to generate representations that can *discriminate* the true resulting state from states reached by alternative actions. This improves the accuracy of downstream ranking models, leading to better web agent performance.
items.figure_caption: Qualitative example of predicted next-state representations at a single decision point in the WebArena Reddit environment. Given the current state and queried action, our predicted-state-matching world model identifies the specific state change produced by the action. A textual-summary method, WebDreamer ( Gu et al., 2025 ) , instead describes the outcome of a different action, while a full structured-state method, WebWorld ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) , emits a long AXTree-style representation that largely repeats page structure unchanged by the queried action. The browser pane is rendered from the recorded accessibility tree.

items.title: Door-in-the-Face Requests and Refusal Behaviour in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether the "door-in-the-face" persuasion technique, where a large refused request increases compliance with a smaller one, applies to Large Language Models (LLMs). The study found that this technique is effective on some LLMs (Anthropic's frontier models) but backfires on others (OpenAI and Google's frontier models), demonstrating that LLMs react differently to concessionary persuasion based on their underlying architecture or training.

items.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
items.abstract: This paper evaluates the coherence of language model probabilistic forecasts by using a procedure based on de Finetti's theorem. It computes the largest possible "Dutch-book profit" an arbitrageur could achieve by betting against the model's predictions, serving as a measure of incoherence. The core contribution is a method to assess forecast coherence without needing observed outcomes, revealing significant incoherence in current language model forecasts.

items.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
items.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of root cause analysis (RCA) in complex telecom networks by proposing a structured reasoning framework for Large Language Models (LLMs). The core method involves grounding LLM diagnostic reasoning with telecom-specific evidence and domain knowledge to overcome issues like hallucination and unstable reasoning. The main contribution is this framework, which aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-driven RCA in telecommunications.

items.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
items.abstract: This paper introduces DisCo, an AI agent designed to distill operational knowledge from GitHub repositories into reusable "skills" for AI agents. The core method involves two distillation approaches: one for creating general-purpose skills from widely used repositories, and another for generating task-specific skills. The main contribution is enabling AI agents to leverage this distilled, human-like know-how, bridging the gap between knowing a method and effectively implementing it for machine learning research.
items.figure_caption: The impact of reusable skills on autonomous research agents. (a) AREX-Skill adds the missing operational layer beyond the model and harness, replacing trial-and-error exploration with reusable procedures that support the task’s operational steps. (b) The skill library and DisCo agent form the resulting stack, and skill augmentation improves performance across four benchmarks.

items.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
items.abstract: Cliff's core method is to use an off-the-shelf LLM to identify the first mistake in a reasoning process rollout. This decomposes the rollout into a correct prefix and an incorrect suffix. The paper's contribution is a reward shaping strategy that converts this signal into token-level advantages, providing more granular guidance for LLM training than traditional outcome-based rewards.

items.title: CodePoisonRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
items.abstract: CodePoisonRAG is a framework for knowledge poisoning attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (RACG). It transforms benign code into poisoned artifacts by injecting specific vulnerabilities and mislabeling them as safe. This allows attackers to propagate chosen weaknesses into generated code without altering the underlying language model.

items.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether tabular foundation models (TFMs) learn physics from data. The core method involves evaluating TFMs against baselines on datasets derived from physical equations. The key contribution is demonstrating that while TFMs excel at interpolating physical relationships, their inherent Bayesian structure prevents them from representing noiseless mechanisms or physical units, thus limiting their ability to truly act as physical models.
items.figure_caption: TFMs interpolate physics but do not learn enough of it to extrapolate. A noiseless damped harmonic oscillator queried beyond the sampled range, against baselines. The oscillation is recovered where there is data and lost immediately outside it. Details and other models in App. A .

items.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
items.abstract: This paper argues that user feedback is a valuable, yet underutilized, signal for improving LLMs, challenging the notion that it's too noisy. Their core method involves comparing LLM revisions made with and without feedback on both synthetic and naturalistic data. The key contribution is demonstrating that feedback-informed revisions significantly outperform baselines in resolving targeted issues, and that current evaluation methods are biased against recognizing this improvement.
